sentences.tr: fa-qālat yā sayyidī wa-ḥabībī wa-qurrata ʿaynī mā taʿlamu annī mutazawwijatun bi-ibni ʿammī wa-anā akrahu ṣūratahu wa-abghuḍu ṣuḥbatahu
sentences.l: So she said: 'O my master, and my beloved, and the coolness of my eye — do you not know that I am married to my paternal-cousin, and I hate his form, and I detest his company?'
sentences.i: She said: 'O my lord, my beloved, and delight of my eye, do you not know that I am married to my cousin, and that I loathe the very sight of him and despise his company?'
sentences.n: قرة عيني, 'the coolness of my eye', is a standing endearment.

sentences.t: وَلَوْلَا أَنِّي أَخْشَى عَلَى خَاطِرِكَ مَا كُنْتُ تَرَكْتُ الشَّمْسَ تَطْلُعُ إِلَّا وَمَدِينَتُهُ خَرَابٌ يَزْعَقُ فِيهَا الْبُومُ وَالْغُرَابُ وَيَأْوِيهَا الثَّعَالِبُ وَ الْذِّئَابُ وَأَنْقُلُ حِجَارَتَهَا إِلَى خَلْفِ جَبَلِ قَافٍ
sentences.tr: wa-lawlā annī akhshā ʿalā khāṭirika mā kuntu taraktu al-shamsa taṭluʿu illā wa-madīnatuhu kharābun yazʿaqu fīhā al-būmu wa-al-ghurābu wa-yaʾwīhā al-thaʿālibu wa-al-dhiʾābu wa-anqulu ḥijāratahā ilā khalfi jabali Qāf
sentences.l: And were it not that I fear for your feelings, I would not have left the sun rise except with his city (being) a ruin, the owl and the raven shrieking in it, and the foxes and the wolves denning in it, and I moving its stones to behind Mount Qaf.
sentences.i: 'And were it not that I fear for your peace of mind, I would not let the sun rise again but I had left his city in ruins, the owl and the raven screeching over it, the foxes and the wolves denning in it, and its very stones carried off beyond Mount Qaf.'
sentences.n: Mount Qaf is the fabled mountain ringing the world in Islamic cosmology, the standard byword for the ends of the earth.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْعَبْدُ تَكْذِبِي يَا مَلْعُونَةُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-ʿabdu takdhibī yā malʿūnah
sentences.l: So the slave said: 'You lie, o accursed one.'
sentences.i: The slave said: 'You're lying, you cursed woman.'
sentences.n: تكذبي stands for Classical تَكْذِبِينَ, 2fs indicative; the final نَ is dropped, as regularly in this text's Middle Arabic.

sentences.t: وَ أَنَا الْعَبْدُ وَ حَقِّ فُتُوَّةِ السُّودَانِ وَ لَا نَظَرَتْ رُوحِي مَرَّةً الْبِيضَانَ مِنْ هَذَا الْيَوْمِ
sentences.tr: wa-anā al-ʿabdu wa-ḥaqqi futuwwati al-sūdāni wa-lā naẓarat rūḥī marratan al-bīḍāna min hādhā al-yawm
sentences.l: And I — the slave — by the truth of the manliness of the blacks — my soul shall not look, ever again, [upon] the whites, from this day.
sentences.i: 'And I — I, the slave, swear by the honor of black men's manhood — my soul will never again look at a white woman from this day forth.'
sentences.n: وحق فتوة السودان is an oath formula, 'by the honor of the blacks' futuwwa (manly virtue)'; the negated perfect لا نظرت after an oath is the idiom for an emphatic vow never to do a thing. البيضان, 'the whites', picks up السودان, 'the blacks', from a few words before.

sentences.t: إِنْ بَقِيتِ تَقْعُدِي إِلَى هَذَا الْوَقْتِ لَا أُصَاحِبُكِ وَلَا أُلْزِقُ جَسَدِي عَلَى جَسَدِكِ يَا مَلْعُونَةُ
sentences.tr: in baqiti taqʿudī ilā hādhā al-waqti lā uṣāḥibuki wa-lā ulziqu jasadī ʿalā jasadiki yā malʿūnah
sentences.l: If you keep staying-seated until this hour, I will not consort with you, nor will I stick my body upon your body, o accursed one.
sentences.i: 'If you go on coming this late, I will have nothing more to do with you, nor press my body to yours again, you cursed woman.'
sentences.n: تقعدي likewise drops the expected نَ of the 2fs indicative.

sentences.t: تَلْعَبِي بِنَا نَشُفُّ أَكُفَّ نَحْنُ عَلَى يَا مُسْتَهْزِئَةُ يَا كَلْبَةُ يَا أَخَسَّ الْبَغَايَا
sentences.tr: talʿabī binā nashuffu akuffa naḥnu ʿalā yā mustahziʾatu yā kalbatu yā akhassa al-baghāyā
sentences.l: Do you play with us — do our hands go dry, we, upon [it]? — o mocking woman, o bitch, o vilest of the whores.
sentences.i: 'Are you toying with us, that we should sit here parched on your account? O mocking woman, you bitch, you vilest of whores!'
sentences.n: The clause تلعبي بنا نشف اكف نحن على is textually obscure — no reading gives fully regular grammar, and a word may be missing or corrupted. نشف most plausibly continues the root ن-ش-ف 'to dry up', suggesting the slave's complaint that the men were left dry (thirsty, or empty-handed) waiting on her — in keeping with the wine mentioned earlier in the night — but the precise sense is a guess. It is vocalized and translated here exactly as printed, on the same footing as ورحاق in the pilot night's closing line. The insults themselves (كلبة 'bitch', اخس البغايا 'vilest of whores') are translated at full coarseness, per house style.

sentences.t: قَالَ فَلَمَّا سَمِعْتُ كَلَامَهُ وَأَنَا أَنْظُرُ وَأَرَي وَأَسْمَعُ مَا جَرَى بَيْنَهُمَا صَارَتِ الدُّنْيَا فِي وَحْشَتِي ظَلَامًا
sentences.tr: qāla fa-lammā samiʿtu kalāmahu wa-anā anẓuru wa-arā wa-asmaʿu mā jarā baynahumā ṣārati al-dunyā fī waḥshatī ẓalāman
sentences.l: He said: 'And when I heard his words — I watching and seeing and hearing what passed between the two of them — the world turned, in my dread, to darkness.'
sentences.i: He went on: 'When I heard his words — for I was watching, seeing, and hearing all that passed between them — the world turned black before me in my horror.'
sentences.n: قال here is the storyteller's tag marking the return to the prince's own first-person account after the slave's quoted speech, as recurs through the Nights. صارت الدنيا ... ظلاما echoes the idiom 'the world turned black' met in the frame story's opening (there اسودت الدنيا في وجهه, 'in his face'); here it turns 'in my وحشة' — a word carrying both 'dread' and 'desolate loneliness'.

sentences.t: عَرَفْتُ رُوحِي فِي أَيِّ مَوْضِعٍ أَنَا وَبِنْتُ عَمِّي
sentences.tr: ʿaraftu rūḥī fī ayyi mawḍiʿin anā wa-bintu ʿammī
sentences.l: I knew my soul (myself), in what place [i.e. plight] I and my paternal-cousin (were).
sentences.i: I saw clearly, then, in what a plight my cousin and I stood.
sentences.n: بنت عمي, 'my paternal uncle's daughter', is the narrator's own wife and cousin, the standing kin-term echoing ابن عمي in the other wife's speech above.

sentences.t: وَقَامَتْ تَبْكِي عَلَيْهِ وَتَتَذَلَّلُ لَهُ وَتَقُولُ لِلْعَبْدِ يَا حَبِيبِي وَثَمَرَةَ فُؤَادِي
sentences.tr: wa-qāmat tabkī ʿalayhi wa-tatadhallalu lahu wa-taqūlu li-al-ʿabdi yā ḥabībī wa-thamarata fuʾādī
sentences.l: And she rose weeping over him and abasing herself to him and saying to the slave: 'O my beloved, and fruit of my heart —'
sentences.i: And she rose weeping before him, abasing herself, and saying to the slave: 'O my beloved, o fruit of my heart —'

sentences.t: إِذَا غَضِبْتَ عَلَيَّ مَنْ يُبْقِينِي وَ إِذَا طَرَدْتَنِي مَنْ يُؤْوِينِي يَا حَبِيبِي يَا نُورَ عَيْنِي
sentences.tr: idhā ghaḍibta ʿalayya man yubqīnī wa-idhā ṭaradtanī man yuʾwīnī yā ḥabībī yā nūra ʿaynī
sentences.l: '— if you are angry at me, who will keep me? And if you drive me away, who will shelter me? O my beloved, o light of my eye.'
sentences.i: '— if you are angry with me, who will keep me? And if you cast me off, who will give me shelter? O my beloved, o light of my eye!'

sentences.t: وَمَازَالَتْ تَبْكِي وَتَتَضَرَّعُ لَهُ حَتَّى رَضِيَ عَلَيْهَا فَفَرِحَتْ
sentences.tr: wa-mā zālat tabkī wa-tataḍarraʿu lahu ḥattā raḍiya ʿalayhā fa-fariḥat
sentences.l: And she did not cease weeping and imploring him until he was pleased with her; and she rejoiced.
sentences.i: And she did not stop weeping and pleading with him until he relented toward her, and then she rejoiced.

sentences.t: وَ قَامَتْ وَقَلَعَتْ ثِيَابَهَا وَلِبَاسَهَا وَقَالَتْ يَا سَيِّدِي مَا عِنْدَكَ مَا تَأْكُلُ جَارِيَتُكَ
sentences.tr: wa-qāmat wa-qalaʿat thiyābahā wa-libāsahā wa-qālat yā sayyidī mā ʿindaka mā taʾkulu jāriyatuk
sentences.l: And she rose and stripped off her clothes and her garments, and said: 'O my master, have you nothing your slave-girl may eat?'
sentences.i: And she rose and stripped off her clothes and garments, and said: 'O my master, have you nothing here for your slave-girl to eat?'
sentences.n: جاريتك — she styles herself 'your slave-girl', in the submissive register of the whole scene. The edition already prints تأكل with its hamza (ء) written out, unlike the many bare alifs elsewhere in this slice, and is kept exactly as printed.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهَا اكْشِفِي اللَّقَنَ تَحْتَهُ عِظَامُ فِيرَانٍ مَطْبُوخَةٌ فَكُلِيهَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahā ikshifī al-laqana taḥtahu ʿiẓāmu fīrānin maṭbūkhatun fa-kulīhā
sentences.l: So he said to her: 'Lift the basin — beneath it are cooked bones of rats — so eat them.'
sentences.i: He told her: 'Lift the basin there — under it are cooked rat-bones; eat those.'
sentences.n: اللقن, a basin or tub, evidently turned over here as a makeshift cover for the food left under it.

sentences.t: وَ قُومِي لِعِنْدِ الْقَدَارَةِ فِيهَا بَقِيَّةُ مَرَارٍ فَاشْرَبِيهَا
sentences.tr: wa-qūmī li-ʿindi al-qadārati fīhā baqiyyatu marārin fa-ishrabīhā
sentences.l: And rise, to at the cooking-pot; in it is a remnant of bitter dregs; so drink it.
sentences.i: 'And go over to the pot — there's a bit of bitter dregs left in it; drink that.'
sentences.n: القدارة, a cooking-pot (a Middle Arabic form beside the more familiar قِدْر). مرار here is the bitter dregs or leavings at the bottom, from the root of مرارة 'bitterness', not a variant of مرق 'broth'.

sentences.t: فَقَامَتْ وَأَكَلَتْ وَ شَرِبَتْ وَغَسَلَتْ يَدَيْهَا وَفَمَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāmat wa-akalat wa-sharibat wa-ghasalat yadayhā wa-famahā
sentences.l: So she rose and ate and drank and washed her hands and her mouth.
sentences.i: So she rose and ate and drank and washed her hands and her mouth.

sentences.t: وَجَاءَتْ رَقَدَتْ مَعَ الْعَبْدِ عَلَى قَشِّ الْقَصَبِ وَتَعَرَّتْ وَدَخَلَتْ مَعَهُ تَحْتَ الْهِدْمَةِ وَالشَّرَامِيطِ
sentences.tr: wa-jāʾat raqadat maʿa al-ʿabdi ʿalā qashshi al-qaṣabi wa-taʿarrat wa-dakhalat maʿahu taḥta al-hidmati wa-al-sharāmīṭ
sentences.l: And she came [and] lay down with the slave upon the straw of the reed, and stripped naked, and went in with him beneath the ragged garment and the tatters.
sentences.i: And she came and lay down with the slave upon the litter of reeds, stripped off her clothes, and crept in with him beneath the filthy rag and its tatters.
sentences.n: قش القصب, reed-straw or rush litter, his bedding; الهدمة والشراميط, his single ragged garment and its tatters, doubled here for grotesque emphasis.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا نَظَرْتُ إِلَى هَذِهِ الْفِعَالِ الَّتِي فَعَلَتْهَا بِنْتُ عَمِّي غِبْتُ عَنِ الْوُجُودِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā naẓartu ilā hādhihi al-fiʿāli allatī faʿalathā bintu ʿammī ghibtu ʿani al-wujūd
sentences.l: And when I looked upon these deeds that my paternal-cousin had done, I vanished from existence.
sentences.i: When I beheld these deeds that my cousin had done, I passed clean out of my senses.
sentences.n: غبت عن الوجود, literally 'I was absent from existence', is the idiom for fainting or losing consciousness.

sentences.t: فَنَزَلْتُ مِنْ عَلَى الْقُبَّةِ وَدَخَلْتُ وَأَخَذْتُ السَّيْفَ الَّذِي جَاءَتْ بِهِ بِنْتُ عَمِّي
sentences.tr: fa-nazaltu min ʿalā al-qubbati wa-dakhaltu wa-akhadhtu al-sayfa alladhī jāʾat bihi bintu ʿammī
sentences.l: So I came down from atop the dome, and went in, and took the sword that my paternal-cousin had brought with her.
sentences.i: So I climbed down from atop the dome, went in, and took up the sword my cousin had brought with her.

sentences.t: وَ سَبَتُّ أَنْ أَقْتُلَ الِاثْنَيْنِ
sentences.tr: wa-sabattu an aqtula al-ithnayn
sentences.l: And I 'sabattu' [resolved?] that I should kill the two of them.
sentences.i: And I resolved to kill the pair of them.
sentences.n: سبت is not a recognized verb meaning 'resolved' in the standard lexicons; the sense required by the following أن أقتل الاثنين is clearly 'I resolved, determined'. It may stand for a corruption of a verb such as بتّ ('I decided firmly', root ب-ت-ت) or عزمت, but is reproduced and vocalized here exactly as printed, its precise form left uncertain — compare the note on ورحاق in the pilot night.

sentences.t: فَضَرَبْتُ الْعَبْدَ أَوَّلًا عَلَى رَقَبَتِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-ḍarabtu al-ʿabda awwalan ʿalā raqabatih
sentences.l: So I struck the slave first, upon his neck.
sentences.i: So I struck the slave first, upon his neck.

sentences.t: فَظَنَنْتُ أَنَّهُ قَدْ قُضِيَ عَلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-ẓanantu annahu qad quḍiya ʿalayh
sentences.l: And I supposed that it had already been decided against him.
sentences.i: And I thought I had finished him.
sentences.n: قضي عليه, literally 'it was decided/decreed against him', is the standing idiom for 'he was done for, finished off'.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka Shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalām
sentences.l: And morning overtook Shahrazad, and she fell silent from speech.
sentences.i: And morning overtook Shahrazad, and she fell silent.
sentences.n: The formula that closes every night in the frame story; it is spoken by the outer narrator (recounting Shahrazad's storytelling), not by the prince, so the voice steps outside his first-person tale for this final line. This printing gives simply عن الكلام, without the fuller عن الكلام المباح found elsewhere in the manuscript tradition; it is reproduced exactly as it stands in the archive.
